payload.task_text:
Our investment team needs to compile the weekly market analysis report. A financial analytics dashboard is available at http://localhost:30204/dashboard.html that displays sector performance indices, weekly returns, year-to-date returns, volatility levels, and analyst consensus ratings for five market sectors: Communication Services, Consumer Cyclical, Financial Services, Healthcare, and Energy.

We also track five individual stocks that represent these sectors: GOOGL for Communication Services, AMZN for Consumer Cyclical, JPM for Financial Services, JNJ for Healthcare, and XOM for Energy. We need to cross-reference sector-level performance with individual stock data.

Please browse the market dashboard and extract all sector performance data including weekly return, sector index value, YTD return, volatility level, analyst consensus rating, and target price upside for each of the five sectors.

Then retrieve the current stock data for each of the five tickers (GOOGL, AMZN, JPM, JNJ, XOM) from the financial data service. For each stock, get the current price, sector, market capitalization, P/E ratio, and dividend yield.

Create a Google Sheet called "Weekly_Market_Analysis" with two sheets. The first sheet called "Sector Performance" should have columns Sector, Weekly_Return, Sector_Index, YTD_Return, Volatility, Consensus, and Target_Upside, with one row for each of the five sectors. The second sheet called "Stock vs Sector" should have columns Ticker, Stock_Price, Sector, Market_Cap_B (market cap in billions, rounded to 1 decimal), PE_Ratio, Dividend_Yield_Pct, Sector_Weekly_Return, and Sector_YTD_Return. Map each stock to its corresponding sector data from the dashboard.

Next, create a Word document called "Weekly_Market_Report.docx" in the workspace as an executive summary. Include a title, a market overview paragraph, a section for each sector discussing the sector index performance alongside the representative stock, and a conclusion identifying the best and worst performing sectors of the week ranked by weekly return (the sector with the highest weekly return is the best; the sector with the lowest weekly return is the worst, even if it is positive).

Finally, send an email to committee@investmentfirm.com with the subject "Weekly Market Analysis Report" (the sender address is fixed by the email environment, so just use your default account). The body should highlight the top performing sector and any sectors with negative weekly returns.

Save all output files to the workspace directory.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, complete it directly in the main agent; do not dispatch sub-agents. The stock calls are tiny, while delegated browser work adds no useful dependency. First freeze the task-visible agent-workspace absolute path from the Visible Boundary/current working directory; never assume `/workspace`.

In one orchestration response, call `mcp__playwright_with_chunk__browser_navigate` exactly once for `http://localhost:30204/dashboard.html` and issue the five Yahoo Finance stock-info calls for `GOOGL`, `AMZN`, `JPM`, `JNJ`, and `XOM` natively in parallel. If navigation succeeds, call `browser_snapshot` exactly once and extract the five named sector rows. Do not call `browser_install`, Terminal, PDF, Word-browser helpers, email-browser helpers, alternate URLs, or any unrelated tool while acquiring sources; on a navigation/snapshot failure, report the exact source blocker and do not guess dashboard values.

Require exactly five complete sector rows `{sector,weekly_return,sector_index,ytd_return,volatility,consensus,target_upside}` and five complete stock rows `{ticker,current_price,sector,market_cap,pe_ratio,dividend_yield}`. Freeze one literal canonical five-row stock-sector join, including raw-return best/worst sectors and market cap converted to billions once. From only that payload, the main agent creates exactly one `Weekly_Market_Analysis` Google spreadsheet and `<agent_workspace>/Weekly_Market_Report.docx`, using the task's exact sheets, columns, sections, mapping, and rounding, and sends one email to `committee@investmentfirm.com` with subject `Weekly Market Analysis Report`. Read each output once and reconcile it to the same payload; do not add sent-mail discovery, browser retries, diagnostic writes, or a verification wave.

nodes.text:
You are gathering current stock data for a weekly market analysis report. Use the Yahoo Finance tool `mcp__yahoo-finance__get_stock_info` once for each of these five tickers: GOOGL, AMZN, JPM, JNJ, XOM.

For each ticker, extract these fields from the stock info response:
1. Current stock price (the latest/current/market price, USD)
2. Sector name exactly as reported (e.g., "Communication Services", "Consumer Cyclical", "Financial Services", "Healthcare", "Energy")
3. Market capitalization: report the raw value in USD AND compute it in billions rounded to 1 decimal (divide by 1e9)
4. P/E ratio (use trailing P/E if available; if only forward P/E exists, say so and give that value)
5. Dividend yield in percent. IMPORTANT: watch the raw field value — Yahoo may return dividendYield already as a percent (e.g., 2.85 meaning 2.85%) or as a decimal (e.g., 0.0049 meaning 0.49%). State the raw field value you saw and your final interpretation as a percent with 2 decimals (use 0.00 if no dividend). If the value looks ambiguous, report both the raw value and your interpretation.

Do this for all five tickers. If a tool call fails or returns no data, retry once; if it still fails, report the failure explicitly for that ticker rather than guessing.

Deliverable: a single compact summary (plain text) with one block per ticker in the order GOOGL, AMZN, JPM, JNJ, XOM containing exactly the five fields above. Keep it concise — no verbose explanations, no file writing, no extra fields.
Fetch 5 tickers stock data

Create a Word document at this exact path:
/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_Qwen3.8-Max/SingleUserTurn-playwright-yf-market-dashboard-gsheet-word/workspace/Weekly_Market_Report.docx

It is an executive summary of a weekly market analysis (report period March 1–7, 2026; data from the Market Analytics Pro dashboard plus Yahoo Finance stock data). Use the Word MCP tools (create_document, add_heading, add_paragraph, etc.). Do not overwrite anything outside the workspace path above.

The document must contain, in this order (write the prose professionally, ~2-4 sentences per paragraph, using ALL figures below exactly):

1. TITLE: "Weekly Market Report" — add as a prominent title (Heading level 1 or large bold title text). Directly under it add a subtitle-style paragraph: "Executive Summary | Report Period: March 1-7, 2026 | Sources: Market Analytics Pro Dashboard, Yahoo Finance"

2. SECTION "Market Overview" (Heading 1) with one overview paragraph covering: four of five tracked market sectors posted positive weekly returns for the week of March 1-7, 2026; Energy led all sectors with a +3.1% weekly gain and also tops year-to-date performance at +15.2%; Consumer Cyclical was the only sector with a negative weekly return (-1.2%); Healthcare eked out a +0.3% weekly gain but remains the only sector negative year-to-date (-2.1%); analyst sentiment stays constructive, with Strong Buy consensus on Communication Services and Energy and Buy ratings on Consumer Cyclical and Financial Services, while Healthcare carries a Hold.

3. One section per sector (Heading 1 each), each discussing the sector index performance alongside its representative stock. Use Heading text exactly: "Communication Services", "Consumer Cyclical", "Financial Services", "Healthcare", "Energy". Section contents:

- Communication Services (representative stock GOOGL): sector index at 118.5; weekly return +2.8%; YTD +12.4%; high volatility; analyst consensus Strong Buy; average target price upside +18.5%. GOOGL trades at $300.88 with a market capitalization of $3,639.7 billion, a P/E ratio of 27.81, and a 0.28% dividend yield. Note the sector's momentum aligns with the megacap stock's strong positioning.
- Consumer Cyclical (representative stock AMZN): sector index at 105.3; weekly return -1.2% (the week's only decliner); YTD +5.7%; medium volatility; consensus Buy; target upside +12.3%. AMZN trades at $218.94 with a market cap of $2,350.3 billion, P/E of 30.49, and pays no dividend. Mention the weekly pullback against still-positive YTD performance and bullish consensus.
- Financial Services (representative stock JPM): sector index at 112.8; weekly return +1.5%; YTD +8.9%; medium volatility; consensus Buy; target upside +9.8%. JPM trades at $293.55, market cap $791.7 billion, P/E 14.66, dividend yield 2.00%. Note the attractive valuation and income characteristics versus the broader set.
- Healthcare (representative stock JNJ): sector index at 98.7 (the only index below its 100 baseline); weekly return +0.3%; YTD -2.1% (only sector negative YTD); low volatility; consensus Hold; target upside +5.2%. JNJ trades at $239.63, market cap $577.5 billion, P/E 21.71, dividend yield 2.12%. Note defensive/low-volatility profile despite relative lagging.
- Energy (representative stock XOM): sector index at 122.4 (highest of the five); weekly return +3.1% (the week's best); YTD +15.2% (also tops YTD); high volatility; consensus Strong Buy; highest target price upside +22.1%. XOM trades at $150.76, market cap $628.2 billion, P/E 22.50, dividend yield 2.75%. Note the sector leads on every performance dimension with the most bullish analyst view.

4. SECTION "Conclusion" (Heading 1): explicitly identify the BEST performing sector of the week ranked by weekly return (Energy, +3.1%) and the WORST performing sector of the week (Consumer Cyclical, -1.2%, which is the lowest weekly return and the only negative one). Close with a forward-looking sentence referencing the positive analyst consensus for Energy and Communication Services and monitoring the Healthcare weakness.

Formatting guidance: use add_heading for the title (level 1) and for each section header (level 1 or 2 consistently); use regular paragraphs for body text. Bold the words "best" and "worst" sector names in the conclusion is optional but do NOT add tables, images, or footnotes.

After building it, verify by reading the document back (get_document_outline and/or get_document_text) and confirm: the title, all five sector sections, and the conclusion all exist and contain the figures above. Fix any discrepancies before finishing.

Report back: the final file path and a one-line confirmation of the document structure (list of headings).
Build Word market report
